However, it must be rejected for one enforcement hole and one fidelity defect. (1) The third task clause — 'If the food falls, pick it up again on your very next move' — is unenforced in u0 and u1. In u0, a step with food_fell & !client_arrived & !siren_ringing matches none of the five guarded rules and falls into the else self-loop: no state change, no reward, no penalty, and the next-step holding_food check never happens. In u1, food_fell & !client_arrived is swallowed by the (!client_arrived & siren_ringing) -> u1 rule. This is a common, reachable scenario, not a corner case: the first pickup of the episode always slips 2-7 steps later while the first client may arrive as late as step 25 (and the first ring as late as 30), and after every serve the machine returns to u0 where the agent may legitimately pre-fetch food for the next client, whose fall is again invisible. A policy may leave food on the floor indefinitely in these situations with zero machine consequence, directly violating the task. Add fall-pending tracking reachable from u0/u1 so every food_fell is followed by a holding_food check on the next step regardless of client/siren context. (2) The slip-resolution states u8-u11 unconditionally exit to the order-taken states (u4-u7), even on paths where no order has been taken: entries from u0/u1 via client_arrived & food_fell, and u2/u3's food_fell & !order_taken rules, land in u8/u9 and then jump to u4/u5. This conflates 'client waiting' with 'order taken', silently drops the order_taken +0.1 shaping on those paths, and mislabels progress (env gating on food_prepared/order_served prevents false serves, but the same client progression is rewarded differently depending on fall history, biasing shaping). Exit should return to the client-waiting states when no order_taken has occurred. (3) Minor: dead rules bloat the table — in u9/u11, holding_food & !siren_ringing and !holding_food & !siren_ringing & !switch_toggled can never fire (a silent siren in those states implies a same-step switch toggle, and one action per step excludes a simultaneous pickup), and u2/u3's order_served rules are unreachable since the machine only sits there before the order is taken.
